items.name: Rusty Sword
items.description: A plain soldier's blade, its edge dulled by years and neglect. Still swings true enough.
items.lore: Watch surplus goes by the crate when the armory clears its racks, and half the cellars in Liscor hold one of these. Somebody drilled with it every morning for a year, once, and then stopped.

items.name: Relc's Spare Spear
items.description: A castoff from the Watch armory, spear-length and Gnoll-sized in the grip. Relc calls it 'barely used' -- for a given value of barely.
items.lore: The Watch quartermaster budgets for Relc the way innkeepers budget for breakage. This one survived him, which means the haft is good and the week was quiet.

items.name: Crude Blade
items.description: Hammered out in a hurry by goblin hands, more wedge than sword. It still cuts.
items.lore: Goblin forges run on scavenge: plow edges, cartwheel rims. Whoever hammered this understood one thing about swords, and it was the edge.

items.name: Chipped Spear
items.description: A goblin spear, its haft wrapped in scavenged cord and its head notched from hard use.
items.lore: The cord on the haft has been rewrapped by three different hands. Goblin gear outlives goblins; it gets passed forward, not down.

items.name: Solid Oak Spear
items.description: A well-balanced practice spear, fire-hardened oak from butt to point. No frills, no rust.
items.lore: Turned out by the dozen for the yard behind the Watch barracks, where recruits learn which end matters. The oak usually outlasts the recruit's pride.

items._comment: GH#70 [Archer]: the T1 weapon of the sword/spear/bow trio -- damage_mod 0, matches rusty_sword/chipped_spear/solid_oak_spear's own T1 curve exactly, but PURCHASABLE (unlike those three, fixture/loot-only starter gear) at the peddler's stall (peddler_stall.json), 8g -- the cheapest weapon in the shop, well under gnollish_hunting_knife's 15g. `range: 4` is the new field this task introduces (absent/1 on every other weapon = melee; see wi_combat.gd's WEAPON_RANGE doc comment).
items.name: Training Bow
items.description: A light practice bow, more suited to a target range than a battlefield. Still puts an arrow where you point it.
items.lore: The peddler's cart carries three or four of these most days, strung and restrung by hands that never quite trust the wood. Nobody buys one to hunt with. Everybody buys one to learn with.

items._comment: GH#70 [Archer]: the T2 upgrade -- damage_mod 1, the gnollish_hunting_knife curve (mundane tier, +1 damage_mod, priced a notch above the T1 weapon) applied to the bow family. Sold at Krshia's stall (krshia_crate.json's 'shop' node, alongside the hunting knife), 18g.
items.name: Hunting Bow
items.description: A proper hunting bow, seasoned and well-strung, built for a hand that already knows which end the arrow goes on.
items.lore: Krshia keeps a few behind the counter for the Gnoll caravans that still hunt the plains the old way. She'll sell one to anyone -- adventurer or otherwise -- who can prove they won't put an eye out.

items.name: Leather Jerkin
items.description: Boiled leather stitched over a linen underlayer. Common wear for anyone who expects to be hit.
items.lore: A tannery south of the market cures these forty at a time, and the smell reaches the gate when the wind turns. New ones go to adventurers; secondhand ones come back from the Floodplains with the stitching checked.

items.name: Watch-Issue Gambeson
items._comment_price: Previously unpriced (no live acquisition path -- fixture/harness-only). Sold at the new street `peddler_stall` (surplus gear, one mini-buy per the market-depth task). Priced against the existing mundane-armor band: leather_jerkin (dr0/+4hp) is 24g, wool_lined_cloak (+3hp) is 18g -- this item trades hp_mod for a full damage_reduction point (a stat the balance harness treats as meaningfully strong, e.g. the dr-2 stack cell), so 20g sits between them rather than under-pricing a defensive stat nothing else in the shop band grants alone.
items.description: Quilted padding stamped with the Liscor Watch's seal. Standard issue for anyone patrolling the walls.
items.lore: Signed out against a deposit, and Watch Captain Zevara knows exactly how many never came back. The padding is older than some of the guards inside it; the budget for replacements has died in council three years running.

items.name: Traveler's Charm
items.description: A weathered trinket found among old stones outside the city, strung on a cord gone soft with age. Something about it settles the nerves.
items.lore: The old stones outside the city give up trinkets like this after a hard rain, and nobody living remembers who strung them. Hold it to your ear and it hums, faintly. Most owners decide not to ask a second question.

items.name: Gnollish Hunting Knife
items.description: A short, wickedly balanced skinning blade from the Silverfang stalls, its bone grip worn smooth by a hunter's hand. Krshia swears by the steel.
items.lore: Silverfang steel comes south with the tribe's caravans and gets worked plains-side, the old way, before it ever sees a city stall. Krshia could sell three times what her kin send her. She says so to anyone who buys one.

items.name: Wool-Lined Cloak
items.description: Heavy travel-weave lined with carded wool, cut for the Floodplains' wet cold. Market goods, honestly priced -- Krshia will remind you of that.
items.lore: Plains wool, city loom: Gnoll caravans sell the fleece and Drake weavers argue the price, and the cloak comes out warmer than the bargaining. The Floodplains rain finds every cheaper seam.

items.name: Copper Luck-Band
items.description: A thin copper ring, polished bright by worried thumbs. Drakes swear copper turns bad luck aside; copper-sellers agree loudly.
items.lore: Every stall in the gate market moves a tray of these. The luck is arguable; the copper is real, and that is the Silverfang position on the matter.

items.name: Hedge-Ward Charm
items.description: Dried herbs and a knot of red thread sealed in a wax bead, warm to the touch. Roadside work, from up north.
items.lore: Hedge-charmers work the wagon stops between Celum and Liscor, selling wards to travelers who want the odds nudged. Most beads are wax and hope; this one was made by somebody with a real Skill, and it knows it.

items.name: Hunter's Fang Talisman
items.description: A beast's fang on a braided cord, capped in silver. The point still looks like it has opinions.
items.lore: The silver fang is the Silverfang mark, and the stall caps a good trophy in it for a hunter who asks. Krshia will tell you whose kill this was if you ask, and the story runs longer than the cord.

items._comment: Issue #89 (gap-2): this record shipped complete (hp_mod/resonance/tier) with no vendor -- an orphaned item. Priced here (20g, between hedge_ward_charm's 9g/hp_mod2 and witch_wardstone_bead's 16g/hp_mod2 -- this carries hp_mod3, the highest of that hp-only tier) and wired as Wilovan's fence stock (invrisil_wilovan.json's 'fence' node): its own lore ('somebody paid them for it, neither name made it back up to the street') is a near-literal match for a fenced good of murky provenance.
items.name: Phosphor Pendant
items.description: A glass bead of sewer phosphor that never quite goes out. Brighter than it has any right to be, and it smells faintly of where it came from.
items.lore: Somebody down in the drains learned to seal the glowing moss in glass, and somebody else paid them for it. Neither name made it back up to the street.

items.name: Stonescale Talisman
items.description: A grey Drake scale, shed and gone stone-hard, set in an iron clasp. Heavier on the mind than on the neck.
items.lore: Shed scales with stone in them turn up in the southern hills, and enchanters pay well for the rare one that takes a binding. Drakes find wearing another Drake's scale distasteful; the stall keeps this one under the counter.

items._comment: Resonance lowered 3 -> 2 (mod values kept). resonance_capacity never grows anywhere in this codebase (fixed default 2, wi_game.gd -- no quest/progression seam mutates it), so a quest-awarded accessory with resonance 3 was structurally unequippable the moment it was granted. The honest minimal fix is capping it at the budget it's actually awarded into, not inventing a capacity-growth mechanic this milestone doesn't have; it still spends the WHOLE budget alone (a deliberate Act-III-capstone trade-off, not a bug).
items.name: Moon-Bone Amulet
items.description: Carved bone on a sinew cord, worn smooth wherever a thumb would rest. Under moonlight the carving is a moon; under anything else it is just circles.
items.lore: Raskghar work, cut in the deep warrens by hands that are only clever some nights. Whatever the amulet waits for, it waits patiently.

items.name: Watch Token
items.description: A brass token stamped with Liscor's gate, the kind the Watch hands to runners and irregulars. It opens no doors by itself, but it slows down the questions.
items.lore: Zevara signs maybe ten of these a year, and she remembers every one. Losing it is a worse conversation than never having earned it.

items._comment: Invrisil 8c Task C3 (issue #13) -- `brothers_marker`, the plan's locked shape 5 vendor/perk gate token (docs/design/dialogue-drafts/invrisil/brothers_lieutenant.json's wiring notes: 'Wood and tin, and worth rather more than its materials'). Granted alongside the accomplishment of the same id (data/dialogue/invrisil_wilovan.json's report option) -- the item is the physical/flavor half, the accomplishment is the gate-checkable half (this game's `requires` gate vocabulary is skill/class/accomplishment/gold only, no item-presence gate, so future fence/vendor content must key off the accomplishment, not this item's inventory presence). watch_token precedent shape verbatim (mundane accessory, zero stat fields).
items.name: Brother's Marker
items.description: Wood and tin, and worth rather more than its materials. Shown in the alleys, trouble steps around you. Shown at the parlor, certain shops stop pretending they don't stock certain things.
items.lore: The Brothers of Serendipitous Meetings hand these out rarely and remember every one they've given. Losing it insults the wrong people.

items.name: Field Whetstone
items.description: A palm-sized whetstone in a leather sleeve, dished from use. Steel forgets its edge; this reminds it.
items.lore: Watch-issue kit includes one, and half the Watch loses theirs by spring. The tanner who sews the sleeves has stopped putting names on them.

items.name: Fisher's Handline
items.description: Waxed line and bone hooks wound on a stick, with a cork float. The Floodplains pond is deeper than it looks.
items.lore: Drakes fish the pond in fair weather and swear off it every winter, when the water starts moving wrong. The line-sellers do their best business in spring, replacing gear that was 'lost.'

items._comment: Issue #59 (the dish-item seam): the hungry patron's Serve option now requires actually FETCHING this from the kitchen (stew_pot's basic_cooking use grants it, wi_game.gd's use_skill) rather than a bare once_per_waking gold-grant. kind:"meal" is the SECOND inert-carried-flavor kind (parcel precedent below) -- no weapon/armor/accessory kind means WIGame.equip() structurally refuses it with zero new code. STRUCTURAL SELLABILITY CALL (WIShop's sellable_items() convention): deliberately NO `price` field at all, same as every parcel -- a plate of stew carried fresh from the kitchen isn't a trade good Krshia would buy back (parcels' own rationale: 'never sold -- no sell surface exists for this kind of carried good'), and omitting the field (rather than authoring `price: 0`) matches the parcel precedent's own structural-exclusion shape instead of a priced-but-worthless item that would need the separate `unsellable` flag (resonant_catalyst's carve-out, reserved for an item that DOES carry a price for its 'Worth N gold' flavor line). Granted by WIGame.use_skill's on_skill_use `item` grant (pickup()), consumed by the patron's Serve dialogue option via the new `remove_item` effect arm -- never stacked, matching every other item in this catalog (cooking again while already holding one is a silent no-op, exactly correct: you don't need two dishes in hand at once).
items.name: Hot Meal
items.description: A bowl of stew and a heel of bread, still steaming from the pot. Someone's waiting on this.
items.lore: The stew pot doesn't care who it's for -- Watch, patron, or the cook themselves. It only cares that it's stirred.

items._comment: GH#68 (Invrisil quest-stage rework, TALK path Stage 2 favor beat): Cups' trust-arc carry item, the #59 item-gate/remove_item seam's second consumer OUTSIDE the delivery board (patron_serving.json's hot_meal precedent, reused for a quest-internal favor rather than a paid Runner's Guild job). kind:"parcel" reused verbatim from the delivery precedent below -- inert carried flavor, no price (never sold), no weapon/armor/accessory kind so equip() structurally refuses it. Granted by invrisil_fixer.json's cups_favor node (a plain dialogue `item` effect, not accept_delivery -- this favor never touches THE DELIVERY BOARD/Vess's counter at all), removed by invrisil_wilovan.json's hub option via `remove_item` on handoff. Never stacked.
items.name: A Debt Chit, Long Overdue
items.description: A folded scrap of paper, Cups' own hand, one line of figures and a name that isn't hers. Worth nothing to sell. Worth plenty to whoever's owed it.
items.lore: Every fixer owes somebody for the corner they work. Cups' somebody wears a hat.

items._comment: 5 parcel items, one per LIVE delivery (docs/design/board-staging/runner-deliveries.json's 6th entry, delivery_hermit_antlers, is a FORWARD-REF -- kept out of data/deliveries.json until HR-II places its destination, so no parcel item ships for it either). kind:"parcel" is INERT carried flavor per the staging doc's own note: no price (never sold -- no sell surface exists in this game), no combat fields, and no weapon/armor/accessory kind means WIGame.equip() structurally refuses it (falls to inventory.gd's generic 'not equippable' toast) with zero new code. Granted by WIGame.accept_delivery via the existing pickup() seam and removed by the new remove_item() seam (on handoff or a sleep-fail return) -- never stacked, matching every other item in this catalog.
items.name: Plains-Wool Bolt
items.description: A bolt of plains-wool, paper-wrapped, smelling of lanolin and a long walk.
items.lore: Runner's Guild delivery parcel (delivery_krshia_wool) -- carried, never worn or sold; removed from the pack on handoff or on a failed run.

items.name: A Parcel That Ticks
items.description: A parcel that ticks. Do not shake. The sender says it is a metronome. The sender laughed.
items.lore: Runner's Guild delivery parcel (delivery_pisces_parcel) -- carried, never worn or sold; removed from the pack on handoff or on a failed run.

items.name: Watch Dispatches
items.description: Watch dispatches, string-tied, sealed thrice. The third seal is the Captain's habit, not protocol.
items.lore: Runner's Guild delivery parcel (delivery_gate_dispatch) -- carried, never worn or sold; removed from the pack on handoff or on a failed run.

items.name: Crate of Lamp-Spirit Phials
items.description: Six glass phials of lamp-spirit for the grate crew, cotton-chocked. If it clinks when you set it down, it is already broken.
items.lore: Runner's Guild delivery parcel (delivery_grate_phials, the FRAGILE variant) -- carried, never worn or sold; removed from the pack on handoff or on a failed run.

items.name: Amentus Fruit Hamper
items.description: A hamper of Amentus blue fruit, straw-packed, the poison cores already cut out. You were told twice.
items.lore: Runner's Guild delivery parcel (delivery_inn_hamper) -- carried, never worn or sold; removed from the pack on handoff or on a failed run.

items._comment: 5 more parcel items, issue #72's generated delivery-pool growth (docs/design/board-staging/generated-candidates.json) -- same inert-carried kind:"parcel" shape as the 5 above, one per new LIVE delivery in data/deliveries.json.
items.name: Bundled Gambesons
items.description: Watch-issue gambesons, three of them, bundled tight and none too soft.
items.lore: Runner's Guild delivery parcel (delivery_barracks_gear) -- carried, never worn or sold; removed from the pack on handoff or on a failed run.

items.name: Sealed Ledger Transfer
items.description: A ledger, sealed, Guild business written on the outside and nothing else.
items.lore: Runner's Guild delivery parcel (delivery_guild_ledger) -- carried, never worn or sold; removed from the pack on handoff or on a failed run.

items.name: Rolled Tactics Brief
items.description: A brief, rolled and string-tied, the ink still faintly damp at the edges.
items.lore: Runner's Guild delivery parcel (delivery_tactics_brief) -- carried, never worn or sold; removed from the pack on handoff or on a failed run.

items.name: A Sealed Letter
items.description: A letter, wax-sealed, no return address, the kind that pays for its own silence.
items.lore: Runner's Guild delivery parcel (delivery_boulevard_letter) -- carried, never worn or sold; removed from the pack on handoff or on a failed run.

items.name: A Sack of Seed Grain
items.description: A sack of seed grain, dense and dry, tied at the neck against damp roads.
items.lore: Runner's Guild delivery parcel (delivery_riverfarm_seed) -- carried, never worn or sold; removed from the pack on handoff or on a failed run.

items.name: Anchor Stone
items.description: A fist-sized stone, warm despite the ruin's cold air, its surface veined with a pattern that never quite resolves into a shape.
items.lore: Warmage Thresk built more than doors, in the end. This one remembers being elsewhere, the same crude trick that woke somewhere it shouldn't have, once, in an inn far from here. Carried, never worn or sold -- it feels like it's waiting to be given back to something.

items._comment_unsellable: Krshia sell mechanic: the only item in this catalog that needs the explicit flag -- it carries a `price` (so it WOULD otherwise leak into WIGame.sellable_items()'s priced-item filter) but its own lore line above already says 'never sold onward'. anchor_stone/brothers_marker/every parcel need no flag (no `price` field at all -- sellable_items() excludes them structurally, same as every other unpriced loot/quest item).
items.name: Resonant Catalyst
items.description: A sliver of worked amber-glass, humming faintly against the palm, wrapped in oiled cloth from under Krshia's counter.
items.lore: A Silverfang trade-route find, sold to the rare customer who asks the right way and pays the whole price without haggling. Krshia doesn't know what it's for. She knows it's worth what she charges for it. Carried, never worn or sold onward.

items._comment: 8b R3 (issue #11) witch-cottage vendor stock, unlocked at blight_lifted (riverfarm_witch.json's 'shop' node). Herb-craft consumables, generic-plausible (not deep TWI canon) per the peddler_stall/Krshia-charms precedent of original mundane/enchanted stock -- prices 4-20g, inside the shipped accessory envelope (hp_mod/resonance match copper_luck_band/hedge_ward_charm's own bounds, no combat mods beyond it).
items.name: Dried Yarrow Bundle
items.description: A fist-sized bundle of dried yarrow, tied off with plain string.
items.lore: Good for a cut, a fever, or an argument with a stubborn wound. The witch grows it along the hollow's own herb rows and sells it the same as any hedge-charmer would, no craft attached.

items.name: Sleeproot Draught
items.description: A corked vial of something dark and bitter-green, steeped from root.
items.lore: Drink it before sleep and the night goes quiet, one way or another. She won't say which way she means, and doesn't charge extra for the ambiguity.

items.name: Hollow Herb Sachet
items.description: Dried herbs sewn into cloth, tied off with a loop of red thread.
items.lore: The same knot the witch wears at her own wrist, sold plain rather than worked -- she says the thread is decoration and the herbs do the settling. Neither claim sounds entirely honest.

items.name: Witch's Wardstone Bead
items.description: A river-smoothed stone, warded and strung on cord without ceremony.
items.lore: She swears it's nothing special, the same way she swears the tea is just tea. It's warm to the touch a full week after you buy it, which is either coincidence or the second lie.

items._comment: Class-foundation pass R5 (2026-07-12): the [Bargain] price_mod's own real, dynamic-priced buy option (riverfarm_witch.json's 'shop' node, appended after the existing 5 options -- see that file's own _comment for why it's a NEW option rather than a retrofit of the existing baked-in-price ones, which qa/scripts/riverfarm_talk.json exact-array pins). Same herb-craft-mundane register/price band as dried_yarrow_bundle/hollow_herb_sachet.
items.name: Pinch of Warding Salt
items.description: A twist of paper holding a pinch of grey-white salt, faintly gritty between the fingers.
items.lore: Thrown across a threshold, it settles whatever's inclined to cross it uninvited. Not much good against anything that was already invited in.

items._comment: Post-Riverfarm attunement purchase (riverfarm_witch.json's 'shop' node, gated on blight_lifted): banks invrisil_attuned alongside the item grant -- dialogue effects compose as separate {gold},{item},{accomplishment} dicts on one option, the resonant_catalyst/bought_catalyst precedent (krshia_crate.json), no new effect machinery. unsellable:true for the same reason as resonant_catalyst: it carries a real price (so sellable_items() would otherwise catalog it) but the lore below already says it's a keepsake -- the 'bought, not found' shape, unlike the found-only anchor_stone (which has no price field at all).
items.name: Invrisil Attunement Stone
items.description: A plain grey stone, palm-sized, humming so faintly you'd miss it if you weren't listening.
items.lore: Eloise's own stock, sold to those bound for the city rather than the hearth. It doesn't point the way so much as remember it. Carried, never worn or sold onward.

items._comment: 8e Phase C 'Papers for Pallass' Stage 2 (controller ruling 2, the GH#65 late-attuning precedent): invrisil_attunement_stone's exact buy-contract shape -- gated on pallass_sponsored (Stage 1, Selys's sponsorship fee) at Krshia's stall (data/dialogue/krshia_crate.json's 'charms' node), banking pallass_attuned alongside the item grant. unsellable:true for the same reason as invrisil_attunement_stone: a real price but the lore below calls it a keepsake.
items.name: Pallass Attunement Stone
items.description: A dense grey-black stone, heavier than its size, faintly warm at the core the way a forge stays warm long after the fire's banked.
items.lore: Krshia's own stock, sold to those bound for the machine city rather than the hearth. It doesn't point the way so much as remember it. Carried, never worn or sold onward.

items._comment: 8d C1 (issue #14) 'What the Seal Kept', the SKILL route's real cost: consumed via a dialogue-side `remove_item` on the dart_slit_a disarm (trapped_halls), the hungry-patron hot_meal precedent (issue #59) applied to a field prop's `on_skill_use` instead of a conversation option -- same remove_item() seam, same possession-gate shape (a plain requires:{item:...} leg). Stocked at the peddler's stall pre-quest (peddler_stall.json) for 3g, the cheapest priced tool in the catalog on purpose (a coin cost, not a wall).
items.name: Trap Kit
items.description: Wax, wire, and a folding pick, wrapped in oilcloth. Cheap enough that adventurers buy three and lose two.
items.lore: Every peddler within a day of Liscor stocks these now -- the Watch started recommending them after the gallery reopened, and word travels fast when word means coin.

items._comment: Issue #81 (exploration & optional content), 'Renn's Old Warhammer' mini-quest: the carry-back-to-owner item, granted by the renns_gear_stash container prop (data/skeleton_scene.json, guild) and removed via renn_hammer.json's turn-in dialogue option (`remove_item`). kind:"parcel" reused verbatim (cups_debt_chit precedent): inert carried flavor, no price (never sold), no weapon_family so equip() structurally refuses it -- it is Renn's hammer, never the player's to wield.
items.name: Renn's Old Warhammer, Backup
items.description: A plain steel warhammer, propped where somebody clearly forgot it.
items.lore: Renn's backup, left leaning against the Guild's back wall on his last kit haul. Carried, never worn or sold; returned to him on handoff.

items._comment: Issue #81 lore-note collectible thread: found-note items reuse the SAME inert kind:"parcel" shape as the delivery/quest carry-items above (never equipped, never sold, no price field) -- the ONE difference is they are never removed once found (no remove_item call site references a note_ id), so they accumulate permanently in `inventory` for src/ui/journal.gd's new Lore section to list (filtered by the `note_` id prefix, the bounty_/delivery_/parcel_ prefix convention this file already uses). Barracks find (spare_kit_crate's sibling prop, note_watch_veteran). Wiki grounding: the Liscor-Antinium war and the peace that followed it are Volume 1-2 background (Klbkch's own presence as a Watch Senior Guardsman is this game's existing proof of that peace, see docs/design/character-profiles.md) -- this note only echoes ALREADY-shipped, already-cited canon obliquely, introduces no new named character or fact.
items.name: A Watch Veteran's Letter, Unfinished
items.description: A half-finished letter on watch-issue paper, the ink gone brown with age.
items.lore: "...tell them the peace held, that's the whole of it some days. The Hive doesn't forget the war any easier than we do, and neither side started the remembering first. Strange to stand watch beside one of them now and mean it when I say I trust him." It stops there, unsigned.

items._comment: Issue #81 lore-note collectible thread: sewers find (note_sewer_surveyor prop). Wiki grounding: general, non-spoiler Liscor civic background only (an aged Drake-built drainage system, a Council that keeps records) -- consistent with what this repo already establishes via the shipped drainage_marker prop ('An old Drake drainage marker... a map of channels two centuries dead') and Jeiss Sielmark's 'Liscor Councilmember' citation in character-profiles.md. No new canon claim, no named character.
items.name: A Sewer Surveyor's Page, Water-Stained
items.description: A single page, water-warped, in a Drake surveyor's hand.
items.lore: "Third cistern holds. Fourth won't, not another winter — the old stonework predates the Council records, which tells you something about who built it and didn't write it down. Recommend the grate crew stop calling it 'the crack' and start calling it a schedule." No follow-up was ever filed.

items._comment: Issue #81 lore-note collectible thread: barracks find (note_old_dread prop, relocated from an original guild placement -- see that entity's own skeleton_scene.json comment for the scene_dynamism re-derivation). Wiki grounding: echoes this repo's OWN already-shipped Raskghar arc (wiki.wanderinginn.com/Raskghar, Volume 5 -- cited in character-profiles.md's Raskghar entry, and acts.json's Act III beat 'the_stirring': 'Something is moving in the dark beneath the city') diegetically, from a resident's superstition rather than omniscient narration. Introduces no new fact past what the game already ships.
items.name: A Ward-Charm Instruction, Copied Twice
items.description: A ward-charm instruction, copied out in two different hands.
items.lore: "Salt at the sill. Don't dig where the ground sounds hollow. If the dogs won't go, you don't go." A later hand added a line underneath, in different ink: "They found something under the city once. They can find it again."

items._comment: Issue #92 (economy depth): boss-unique drop, THE VAULT (vault_boss_slot, data/maps/dungeon/trapped_halls.json, one-time -- no `respawns` key), via `WIEconomy.roll_loot` (isolated hash(run_seed,encounter_id) rng, never the live combat stream). Existing accessory shape verbatim (moon_bone_amulet's own dr+hp+resonance-2 curve, no new fields); no `price` (loot-only, no established vendor worth -- the moon_bone_amulet/watch_token precedent for a one-of-a-kind find).
items.name: Construct Core Shard
items.description: A fist-sized shard of the Vault Construct's own core, still faintly warm, its inner light gone dim but not dark.
items.lore: Warmage Thresk's vault work outlived the war it was built for, and so, it turns out, did the thing built to guard it. Whatever kept it standing three centuries in the dark keeps standing a while longer in a pocket.

items._comment: Issue #92: boss-unique drop, the trapped-halls snare fight (snare_nest_slot, same map, one-time -- no `respawns` key). Existing accessory shape, hedge_ward_charm's own hp+resonance-1 curve (mid-tier, matches the fight's mid-delve placement between the mundane starter loot and the Vault's own capstone drop above).
items.name: Warded Coil Charm
items.description: A twist of warding-wire salvaged from the snare itself, the working still humming faint and wrongly patient.
items.lore: The wards down here were never meant to be worn -- somebody unwound one anyway and found the working held. It still expects a trespasser. It will have to make do with you.

items._comment: Issue #92: boss-unique drop, kingslayer_den (data/maps/dungeon/dungeon_approach.json, `respawns:true` apex-predator cull -- chance-gated in the map's own loot table, unlike the two guaranteed one-time drops above, matching the crude_blade/chipped_spear repeatable-farm precedent). Existing accessory shape, hunters_fang_talisman's own dmg+resonance-1 curve widened by +1 hp_mod (apex-tier differentiation from that mundane-region trophy).
items.name: Kingslayer Fang
items.description: A single fang, longer than a hand, drawn from the dark the gallery's silk led back to. The point is still sharp enough to matter.
items.lore: Whatever nests south of the gallery has fangs enough to spare one and never notice. Krshia would call this Silverfang-caliber trophy work, if Krshia had ever seen the thing it came from.
